clue.text: Bar German sausage

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A drinking bar serves a German sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but here it is the verb meaning to prohibit. A BANGER is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is everyday British slang for a pork link, so named because it can burst while frying.

clue.text: An impressive type, with courageous countenance

parts.note: a courageous person is bold
countenance means the face

explanation.surface: Someone striking, with a brave look on their features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person, but it is printing type: boldface letters stand out on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, heavy-weighted lettering is called boldface, and it makes a strong visual impression.

clue.text: It enables him to make a clean sweep

definitions.text: It enables him to make a clean sweep

parts.words: It enables him to make a clean sweep
parts.note: plays on the proverb that a newly appointed manager sweeps away old ways, as fresh bristles sweep cleanly

explanation.surface: A tool that lets a cleaner clear everything away.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a new broom sweeps clean' describes a newcomer in charge who makes sweeping changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh brush sweeps the floor clean, and figuratively a newcomer in authority makes radical changes.

clue.text: Always irreverent at heart

indicators.note: at heart points to letters taken from the middle of the word irreverent

explanation.surface: Someone who is perpetually disrespectful deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever and always are synonyms meaning at all times.

clue.text: A fool gets support for dissemination of left-wing views

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: An idiot gains backing for spreading socialist propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is a mild British insult for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop, from agitation and propaganda, is political, especially communist, messaging spread through art and literature.

clue.text: Acquire money to become socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Getting cash in order to fit into society.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means getting hold of currency; idiomatically, an idea that gains currency becomes widely accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, to obtain cash; idiomatically, an idea that spreads and wins general acceptance is said to do this.

clue.text: Steal a roll of film

explanation.surface: Pinching a reel of camera film.
explanation.walkthrough: In filming, each recorded attempt at a scene is called a take.
explanation.definitionFit: To take can mean to steal; in cinema, a single continuous shot recorded by the camera is also called this.

clue.text: I had to enter the arena at the horse-show

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the word for arena

parts.note: a ring is an arena, as at a circus or show
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A competitor has to go into the arena at an equestrian event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' shortens to I'D, which goes inside RING. The definition describes the activity seen at a horse-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsemanship on horseback is the activity displayed at an equestrian show.

clue.text: Father has the sulks, sweetie

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Dad is in a bad mood, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' is an old phrase for being sulky. POPPET is a British term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British endearment for a darling, often a child.

clue.text: Advocate taking egg-producer around Wales

indicators.note: around means the egg-producer's word wraps about the letter for Wales

parts.note: a layer is a hen that produces eggs
W is the abbreviation for Wales

explanation.surface: A barrister takes a hen on a trip round Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' could be a verb, but it is the noun for a legal representative.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a legal professional who pleads cases in court, a synonym for attorney.

clue.text: Recovered, by the helicopter rescue team?

explanation.surface: Someone was saved, winched up by an air rescue crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Recovered as in getting better, and literally lifted into the helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be improving in health is to have rallied; a person winched into a rescue helicopter has been lifted aloft.

clue.text: Just a male manicurist, but he's indispensable

parts.note: just means right, fair
jokingly, a man who works on hands is a hand man

explanation.surface: Only a man who does nails, but he's vital to the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but it means fair or correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a most trusted assistant, someone a leader cannot do without.

clue.text: Fellow confronts anger and passion

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: A man faces fury and strong emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is used for ardour or intense feeling, as in a speech full of fire.

clue.text: About 2.54 centimetres? Sure thing!

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
an inch is exactly 2.54 centimetres

explanation.surface: Roughly an inch long? Certainly!
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is a certainty or something very easy.

clue.text: A number backed Anglicans in the past

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation for a number is reversed

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A numerous group once supported the Anglican church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Children can be a bone of contention

explanation.surface: Kids can cause arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language, and also a matter in dispute.

clue.text: Stop top secretary getting employment

parts.note: a PA, a personal assistant, is a senior secretary
employment means use, as in putting something to work

explanation.surface: Halt the senior assistant from getting a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a brief halt or break in activity.

clue.text: Go over to repair the car's doors

indicators.note: to repair is to fix, so these letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic's errand: fix the vehicle's doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' looks like 'go to', but it is the anagram signal on THE CAR'S DOORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a street from one side to the other is to make it over to the far kerb.

clue.text: Exhausted by the sound of a funeral drum

definitions.text: the sound of a funeral drum

explanation.surface: Worn out by a mournful drumbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead-beat means utterly tired; a funeral drum beats for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-beat is British for utterly tired; jokingly, a beat played for the deceased.

clue.text: A body-builder develops a heavenly body

parts.note: steroids are drugs used to build muscle

explanation.surface: A muscleman develops a godlike physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' looks like praise for a physique, but it is a space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky object orbiting the sun, a celestial object.

clue.text: No mercy shown to Boaz's wife without a cape

parts.note: in the Bible, Ruth married Boaz
without means less, lacking
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A biblical woman is shown no pity because she lacks a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment, but it is a headland (NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring place names).
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthlessness is the quality of having no pity or compassion.

clue.text: Silent resolution to join forces

indicators.note: resolution is the working out of something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A quiet decision to sign up together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join forces' reads as 'cooperate', but here it means sign up for the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service, entering the forces.

clue.text: Large vat Leonard brought up from way underground

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means Leonard's short name is read upwards

parts.note: Len is short for Leonard

explanation.surface: Leonard hauls a big barrel up from deep below.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel is a passage dug beneath the ground.

clue.text: Refusal to join American intelligence

parts.note: no is a refusal
US means American

explanation.surface: Declining to join the US intelligence services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' suggests spies, but it means common sense; NOUS is British informal for practical wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for common sense or practical wisdom.

clue.text: Skate held in reserve

explanation.surface: Skating equipment is kept as a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skate' looks like the boot, but it is the fish, kept chilled at the fishmonger's.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish such as skate are stored chilled on a slab; idiomatically, plans put aside for later are suspended for now.

clue.text: As a painted ship upon a painted ocean (Coleridge)

definitions.text: As a painted ship upon a painted ocean (Coleridge)

parts.words: As a painted ship upon a painted ocean (Coleridge)
parts.note: the line from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner is completed by the missing word that describes the becalmed ship

explanation.surface: A quotation describing a becalmed ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge wrote 'As idle as a painted ship / Upon a painted ocean': the answer is the word the clue leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: A becalmed ship going nowhere is inactive, motionless, doing nothing.

clue.text: Check support

explanation.surface: Verify the backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to halt or delay, as in a stay of execution; a stay is also a brace or rope holding up a mast.

clue.text: When washed it may be hard to dry

definitions.text: When washed it may be hard to dry

parts.words: When washed it may be hard to dry
parts.note: describes what grows on the head and takes a towel or blower after shampooing

explanation.surface: Some laundry takes ages to dry after washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick locks on the head can take a long time to dry after shampooing.

clue.text: Changes I mention almost immediately

indicators.note: changes means the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that changes happen very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, with hardly any delay.

clue.text: Look upon a lad endlessly from the belvedere

parts.note: to gaze is to look

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for a lad loses its final letter

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: Watch a young man from a garden lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a structure built to give a view, like a summerhouse or pavilion.

clue.text: Keeping the score by agreement

explanation.surface: Keeping count of points by mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By agreement' means in agreeing, and to tally is to correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: To tally is to count points; figures that tally correspond or match each other.

clue.text: Coppers rebuked for having blabbed

parts.note: coppers are small coins, pence, abbreviated P
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Policemen were reprimanded for talking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police, but it is copper coins, pence (P).
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter foolishly at length.
